newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto transit service shut down due to protest.
newsitem.headline: Toronto transit service shut down due to protest.

text.p: Transit service in Toronto was shut down on Friday due to labor protests in Canada's biggest city and financial capital, the Toronto Transit Commission said in a statement.
The TTC said that picket activity at its underground train and bus facilities had increased since early this morning.

"The 8:30 a.m. (EDT/1230 GMT) subway delay may be extended further, subject to the degree of picket activity and the aggressive nature of the picket lines," the TTC said. Thousands of protesters were expected to hit the streets today to rally against deep budget cuts by Ontario's Conservative government.
Toronto's bus and subway system handles more than one million commuters a day.

In a bid to paralyze this city of 2.2 million people, organizers planned to close businesses and disrupt services, including Toronto's Pearson Airport, the country's busiest airport. Airport officials said picket lines had not affected service.

"It's pretty much normal. We have some demonstrators, but it hasn't impacted on our operations," said airport spokesman Bruce Reid. Airport officials won a court injunction to ensure essential workers could get through picket lines.
